hub.speaker: Master Coyle
hub.text: A new face. I do like a new face — they're cheap, and occasionally they appreciate into something useful. Browsing, or selling?

text_variants.text: Come to inventory the wreckage? The Guild took the charter, the criers took the rest. I hope the hat-people paid you in something that keeps.
Ah. My consultant. Your retainer is current and your silence is appreciated. My door — regrettably — is always open to you. Wine?

options.text: You framed a man for your own commission.
Your blades are groaning on a warehouse floor. Say it plainly this time.

accusation.speaker: Master Coyle
accusation.text: You've a story, and no idea where it's set. Where does this 'theft' supposedly run out of, consultant? You've gone quiet. I thought as much. Come back when you've walked the ground, and we'll discuss reputations properly.

text_variants.text: Do you know what reputation costs in this city? More than you. Considerably more than him. Whoever sold you that story priced your discretion like an amateur and never thought to price mine at all. So. Prove it, or price your next words very carefully.

options.text: Your own ledger prices it. Forty gold to a 'removal man' — dated the night before your theft.
Cups will swear to the hiring. So will Hellam — you soured his lease, and he kept the receipts.
(Draw steel.) Then we settle it here and now.

cornered.speaker: Master Coyle
cornered.text: That was a better hand than I priced you for. Sit down. Please. Let us speak as adults who know what things cost. Yes — I paid for the removal; the frame was simply cheaper than the fee. Farley's sort are priced by the dozen — warehouse math, a line in anyone's book. To price me you would need the city, and the city hasn't finished paying. So. Name yours. Everyone has one, and today I am buying above market.

text_variants.text: Enough. You've made your point in bruises — a currency I accept, though I do not respect it. Yes. I paid for the removal, and the frame was simply cheaper than the fee. There. Plainly said. Now sit down and let us discuss what your silence costs. I will open with wine and a number, and you may argue with the number.

options.text: Not for sale. The ledger goes to the Watch, the Guild, and every crier with working lungs.
Forty gold — the removal-man's rate. A retainer, and Farley's charges evaporate by morning.

ending_exposed.speaker: Master Coyle
ending_exposed.text: Wait. No. No, you actually mean it. You held a fortune in your hand just now and you're going to burn it — for your Mister Farley, a man in a cheap hat you've never shared a drink with. I have bought forty people in that chair. I want it noted that I offered. Get out. Go be expensive somewhere else.

options.text: The criers will explain the rest.

ending_extorted.speaker: Master Coyle
ending_extorted.text: Forty. Done. Worth it, too, which annoys me more than the sum. The charges were always mine to un-make; watch how fast this city forgets a theft once a rich man yawns. A genuine pleasure, consultant. I prefer enemies with prices. Friends run so very much dearer.
